results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. According to VFB, the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch. VFB holds various records related to the mushroom body, including neurons with some part in the mushroom body, parts of the mushroom body, and images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body. For further information, you can explore the available data, such as the [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") records of neurons with some part in the mushroom body, or the [22137](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in mushroom body") images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain include [[KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [[Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), as well as alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which can be further subdivided into subtypes such as core/surface/posterior, anterior-posterior/middle, and dorsal/main/gamma-s/gamma-t classes. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") records of subclasses of Kenyon cell, indicating the diversity of Kenyon cell types. To explore these types further, you can examine the [31468](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of Kenyon cell") available images of Kenyon cell, scRNAseq data for Kenyon cell, or transgene expression in Kenyon cell, all of which are available in VFB.

results.response: The primary neurotransmitter used by mushroom body Kenyon cells is acetylcholine, as indicated by VFB neurotransmitter tags. VFB holds various data related to [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), including a large number of images, subclasses, scRNAseq data, transgene expression data, and both downstream and upstream connectivity classes. results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn. This information comes from the VFB database, which describes antennal lobe projection neurons sending synaptic output to the mushroom body and lateral horn. VFB holds data on neurons with some part in antennal lobe, including those with synaptic terminals, presynaptic terminals, and postsynaptic terminals, which may be relevant for a narrower follow-up of these connections. Specifically, VFB records show that antennal lobe projection neurons describe axons to higher brain centers, generally the mushroom body calyx and/or lateral horn.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
VFB has annotated [9413](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047887,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central brain") neuron types with some part in the [adult central brain](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047887 "Open adult central brain in Virtual Fly Brain"). The verbatim information from VFB states "Neurons with some part in adult central brain: 9413". Additionally, VFB records show more than 125,000 neurons, as indicated by VFB reference. However, it is essential to note that the "neurons with some part here" figure represents the number of neuron types annotated in VFB, not the biological total. For a published biological total, a citation is required, which is not provided in the available evidence for the adult central brain.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- more than 125,000 neurons (adult Drosophila central brain connectome/model) — A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing. — PMID 39358519
- ~139,255 neurons (whole adult Drosophila brain) — Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. — PMID 39358518

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

results.title: Circuit motif
results.question: Describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs). Which DAN types connect to which MBON types?
results.response:
To describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and which dopaminergic neuron types connect to which MBON types, we can look at the available data in VFB. VFB holds data on the upstream connectivity classes for both [adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049839 "Open adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") and [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") (MBON), with [1290](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00049839,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") and [2077](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") records, respectively. Additionally, VFB has annotated downstream connectivity classes for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron and MBON, with [316](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00049839,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") and [2788](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") records, respectively. 

The connectome data indicates that adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons provide dopaminergic input to MBONs. However, the specific types of dopaminergic neurons and their connections to particular MBON types are not detailed in the information provided here. For detailed information on which types of adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons connect to specific types of MBONs, further query of the upstream and downstream connectivity classes in VFB would be necessary. VFB does not currently hold specific data on the connections between [larval mushroom body dopaminergic neuron h1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111634 "Open larval mushroom body dopaminergic neuron h1 in Virtual Fly Brain") and MBONs in the context provided.

results.response: The connectivity of olfactory projection neurons in the Hemibrain and FAFB connectome datasets is not directly comparable based on the available information. VFB holds data on neurons connected to [oviEN (FAFB:1259226)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_001013vk "Open oviEN (FAFB:1259226) in Virtual Fly Brain") ([50](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=VFB_001013vk,NeuronNeuronConnectivityQuery "Run in VFB: Neurons connected to oviEN (FAFB:1259226)") records), as well as extensive data on olfactory projection neurons, including downstream and upstream connectivity classes ([2819](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00051298,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for olfactory projection neuron") and [1560](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00051298,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for olfactory projection neuron") records, respectively). Additionally, VFB contains numerous images and datasets related to [JRC_FlyEM_Hemibrain](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_00101384 "Open JRC_FlyEM_Hemibrain in Virtual Fly Brain") ([97](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=VFB_00101384,PaintedDomains "Run in VFB: Painted domains for JRCFIB2018Fum") painted domains, [43944](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=VFB_00101384,AllAlignedImages "Run in VFB: All images aligned to JRCFIB2018Fum") aligned images, and [130](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=VFB_00101384,AllDatasets "Run in VFB: All available datasets") available datasets). results.title: Reagent identification
results.question: I want to image neurons in the lateral horn. What split-GAL4 driver lines are available that target lateral horn neuron types?
results.response:
To image neurons in the lateral horn, you can use split-GAL4 driver lines that target lateral horn neuron types. VFB records show that several split-GAL4 driver lines are available for this purpose, with [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00048293,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in LHN") records of transgene expression in the [adult lateral horn neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00048293 "Open adult lateral horn neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). The expression patterns of these driver lines, such as P{DAT-B-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{ple-p65.AD.TH-F} and P{DAT-B-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{ple-p65.AD.TH-D}, are available in VFB. 

For more information, you can explore the available data in VFB, which includes [23150](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00048293,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of LHN") images of the adult lateral horn neuron, [1374](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00048293,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of LHN") subclasses of the adult lateral horn neuron, [6377](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00048293,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for LHN") downstream connectivity classes, and [5933](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00048293,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for LHN") upstream connectivity classes. 

The adult lateral horn neuron has dendritic arbors in the lateral horn and receives olfactory input from antennal lobe projection neurons, according to VFB.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The LPLC2 visual neuron type is known to detect looming (expansion) stimuli and elicit a jump escape response, as reported by Klapoetke et al. (2017) and Wu et al. (2016). VFB records show that it has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. However, VFB does not currently hold specific data on the exact location of LPLC2 visual neuron type beyond its presence in the lobula plate. 

The connectome data indicates that the LPLC2 visual neuron type is involved in initiating a jump escape response, but VFB does not currently hold detailed information on its specific connections. 

The function of the LPLC2 visual neuron type, as described by Klapoetke et al. (2017) and Wu et al. (2016), is to detect looming stimuli, which in turn elicits a jump escape response. VFB holds information on the LPLC2 visual neuron type, including its role in detecting expansion stimuli.

results.title: Comparative anatomy

results.response: The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") in adult Drosophila has approximately 50 glomeruli, whereas in larval Drosophila it has around 22 glomeruli, indicating that the [adult antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007401 "Open adult antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") is more elaborated than the larval antennal lobe, as recorded in VFB. VFB holds various records related to the antennal lobe, including images, neurons with some part in the antennal lobe, and parts of the antennal lobe, with counts of [6](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of antennal lobe") images, [676](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in antennal lobe") neurons, and [100](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of antennal lobe") parts, among others. To further compare the organisation of the antennal lobe between adult and larval Drosophila, you can explore the available data, such as the images of neurons with some part in the antennal lobe, which totals [17046](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe") images, or the neurons with synaptic terminals in the antennal lobe, with [673](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in antennal lobe") records.

results.title: Bidirectional connectivity
results.question: Are there reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and dopaminergic neurons (DANs)? Which pairs have the strongest mutual connectivity?
results.response:
The connectome data indicates that there are reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons. VFB records show 22 reciprocal class-level pairs between these two neuron types. The direction from [dopaminergic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005131 "Open dopaminergic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") to [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") has a higher weight, with a target-to-source weight of 7620, compared to a source-to-target weight of 2697 in the other direction. 

VFB has annotated a large number of connectivity records for both mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons, including downstream and upstream connectivity classes. For mushroom body output neurons, VFB holds [2788](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") records of downstream connectivity classes and [2077](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") records of upstream connectivity classes. For dopaminergic neurons, VFB holds [8845](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neuron") records of downstream connectivity classes and [7914](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neuron") records of upstream connectivity classes.

To identify the specific pairs with the strongest mutual connectivity, you can explore the top_partners listed in the VFB findings on reciprocal connectivity between mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons.

results.title: Connectivity strength comparison
results.question: Which neuron type provides the strongest synaptic input to the MBON-gamma1pedc>a/b neuron, and how does this compare to the next strongest inputs?

results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response:
The anatomical containment hierarchy from the [antennal lobe glomerulus DA1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003932 "Open antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 in Virtual Fly Brain") up to the top-level brain structure is: antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain, as indicated by VFB. 

VFB holds data on the antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, including neurons with some part in it, synaptic terminals, presynaptic and postsynaptic terminals, images of neurons, and transgene expression. Specifically, VFB has annotated [10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, 10 neurons with synaptic terminals in it, [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") neurons with presynaptic terminals, and [8](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") neurons with postsynaptic terminals. Additionally, there are [911](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 and [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") records of transgene expression in it. 

To further explore the hierarchy, you can query VFB for the adult antennal lobe, adult deutocerebrum, adult cerebrum, adult central brain, and adult brain, to find more information on their composition, connections, and related data.

results.response:

VFB does not currently hold specific data on the neural circuit underlying CO2 avoidance in Drosophila. However, VFB holds a large collection of neuroanatomical data and connectivity information for Drosophila, which can be used to identify potential candidate neurons and their connections.

The connectome data indicates that Drosophila has a complex neural network with many interconnected neurons. VFB records show that some neurons in the antennal lobe and the ventral nerve cord are potentially involved in sensing and processing CO2 information. results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as described by Thomas and Wyman (1984). VFB records show that the giant fiber neuron has a distinct anatomy and connectivity. 

VFB holds [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of the giant fiber neuron, which can be used to visualize its anatomy. Additionally, VFB has annotated [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in the giant fiber neuron, which may be useful for understanding its function and identifying available driver lines. 

The connectome data indicates that the giant fiber neuron has downstream connectivity classes ([361](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records) and upstream connectivity classes ([435](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records), which can be used to understand its connectivity. 

For more information on the giant fiber neuron, including its expression pattern and associated GAL4 drivers, VFB and VFB outputs may be useful. Relevant publications, such as Thomas and Wyman (1984), can provide further insight into the giant fiber neuron's role in jump escape behavior.

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response:
The connectome data indicates that neuron types such as [ML-VPN2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052139 "Open ML-VPN2 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052141 "Open Mt-VPN1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052140 "Open Mt-VPN in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mti](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052142 "Open Mti in Virtual Fly Brain"), and T4ai might mediate a connection between the [visual system](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047735 "Open visual system in Virtual Fly Brain") and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB records show that adult visual projection neurons, which have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, could also mediate this connection, as noted by Vogt et al., 2016. 

VFB holds records of neurons with some part in the visual system ([1046](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047735,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in visual system")) and neurons with some part in the mushroom body ([602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body")), as well as neurons with presynaptic and postsynaptic terminals in both the visual system and the mushroom body. This suggests that visual information could potentially reach the memory circuit via these neuron types. 

To further investigate the connection between the visual system and the mushroom body, you can explore the available VFB data, including the tracts/nerves innervating the mushroom body ([14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,TractsNervesInnervatingHere "Run in VFB: Tracts/nerves innervating mushroom body")) and the expression patterns overlapping the mushroom body ([23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ExpressionOverlapsHere "Run in VFB: Expression patterns overlapping mushroom body")).

results.title: Comparative analysis

results.response: The downstream targets of [s-LNv](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch03yp "Open s-LNv in Virtual Fly Brain") and [l-LNv](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fws "Open l-LNv in Virtual Fly Brain") include several neuron types. These shared target classes include adult interneuron, adult cholinergic neuron, adult GABAergic neuron, adult glutamatergic neuron, adult octopaminergic neuron, adult dopaminergic neuron, and adult serotonergic neuron. VFB holds data on these shared downstream targets, which can be explored further to understand the connectivity between s-LNv, l-LNv, and their target neurons.
